name: Orthographic noise
instruction: Score 0–10 for spelling errors, grammatical slips, missing capitalization or punctuation, malformed words, run-ons, or unusual spacing; score only the amount of noise, not its quality or humor.

name: Reference transformation
instruction: Score 10 when a familiar person, text, slogan, or genre is repurposed into a fresh comic mechanism; score 0 when the reference is decorative or simply repeated.

name: Idiom or set-phrase reinterpreted literally
instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the punchline works by taking a common idiom or fixed phrase and reinterpreting it literally in an unexpected context. 10 = the entire joke hinges on a familiar idiom being taken literally. 0 = no idiom is invoked or literalized.

name: Teller as butt, with the admission doing comic work
instruction: Score whether the narrator turns the joke on themselves AND the self-indictment is the payoff rather than a hedge. 10 = the speaker confesses something unflattering about their own habits, taste, or competence, and that confession is the funniest element in the item. 5 = self-deprecation is present but ornamental, an apology attached to a joke that works without it. 0 = no self-reference, or self-reference used purely to pre-excuse weak material.

name: Vivid absurd specificity
instruction: Score 10 when unusual concrete details create a memorable mental image that directly supports the punchline; score 0 when details are generic, decorative, or unrelated to the joke.

name: Era anchoring
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text contains dated public figures, events, platform conventions, current-affairs references, or period-specific slang and idiom; do not judge topicality or whether the feature or joke is good.

name: Named topical/political figure or current-event reference
instruction: Score 0-10 the extent to which the item names or clearly identifies a real, contemporaneously salient public figure, politician, or newsworthy event. 0 = no such reference, 10 = the entire joke is built around and requires recognizing the named figure/event. Do not judge whether referencing them is clever or in good taste.

name: Nothing in the text is removable
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the text is load-bearing: every clause either plants something the ending uses or is required to make the situation legible. 10 = removing any clause breaks the joke; 0 = whole sentences could be deleted without the joke changing. Judge necessity, not brevity -- a long text in which everything is used scores high.

name: Overall length of the post
instruction: Score 0-10 for how long the text is. 10 = many sentences or paragraphs; 5 = a few sentences; 0 = a single short line. Judge extent only -- do not consider whether the length is warranted, whether the build is worth it, or whether anything in it lands.

name: Repost/familiarity framing (retelling-chain position)
instruction: Score 0-10 how much the text explicitly signals that the joke or its form has circulated before -- e.g. labeling itself a repost, apologizing for repetition, referencing a joke number/count, or presupposing the audience already knows the joke -- versus presenting itself as newly composed. 0 = no such signal, 10 = the text is primarily framed around its repost/familiarity status. Score only the presence of this framing, not whether the underlying joke is actually stale or fresh.

name: Reveal forces a rereading of the setup
instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the ending makes the reader go back and reinterpret what the setup meant -- the setup supported one reading, and the last move shows a second reading was there all along. 10 = the whole setup flips meaning on the final move; 0 = the ending adds information but nothing earlier is re-read. Judge the mechanism, not whether the joke amused you.

name: Audience-management furniture: apologies, disclaimers, hedges, requests
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of non-joke servicing text addressed to the reader about the post itself: apologies ('sorry'), self-deprecating disclaimers about the poster or the post, pre-emptive predictions about the post's reception, content warnings, tags, edit notes, 'first post' or 'long-time lurker' framing, and any request or anti-request directed at the readership. 0 = the item is entirely joke with no meta-commentary; 10 = a substantial share of the characters are furniture wrapped around the joke. Measure how much of the text is furniture; do NOT judge whether the furniture is endearing or irritating, and do not judge the joke.

name: Taboo-register intensity
instruction: Score 0–10 for the extent of sexual, scatological, violent, religiously provocative, death-related, or slur-adjacent material; judge only taboo intensity, never whether its use is effective or funny.

name: Surprise from withholding the expected punchline
instruction: Score how much the text sets up an obvious punchline and then deliberately refuses to deliver it (or delivers something else), making the refusal itself the joke. 10 = the expected line is clearly implied but withheld; 0 = punchline delivered normally.

name: Template commitment
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text follows a conspicuous stock joke scaffold such as a question-and-answer, dialogue labels, numbered steps, or a 'what do you call/because' frame; do not judge whether the feature or joke is good.

name: Surprise-coherence balance
instruction: Score 10 when the punchline is genuinely unexpected but becomes retrospectively inevitable from the setup; score 0 when it is predictable or feels like an unrelated non sequitur.

name: Incompleteness: setup with no payoff or pun with no setup
instruction: Score how much the text fails to deliver either a setup or a payoff. 10 = clearly missing one half entirely (truncated or abandoned); 0 = both setup and payoff are present and connected.

name: Concrete image-bearing detail rather than abstract assertion
instruction: Score the specificity of what the reader is asked to picture. 10 = the joke supplies particular, unexpected, physically imaginable detail (a named object, a count, a body, a place) that the payoff then uses. 5 = ordinary concreteness, nothing vivid. 0 = the item is an abstract generality about people or feelings with nothing to picture, or the text has no interpretable referent at all.

name: Wordplay with homophone or near-homophone pivot
instruction: Score how much the humor depends on a word sounding like another word with a different meaning. 10 = the entire joke is built around one homophone the reader must hear; 0 = no phonetic ambiguity is used.

name: Verbosity and setup-to-punch bulk
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of the text's bulk and elaboration, independent of content: total length, number of sentences, amount of scene-setting or narrative build before the final line, presence of dialogue turns, line breaks, paragraph breaks, embedded quotation blocks, enumerated steps or lists. 0 = a single short clause or one-liner under roughly fifteen words; 5 = two to three sentences or a short two-turn exchange; 10 = a multi-paragraph build, extended narrative, or long quoted block. Score length and structural elaboration only. Do NOT judge whether the length is earned, whether the build pays off, or whether brevity is a virtue here.

name: Forum-aware framing
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text explicitly references the subreddit, commenters, front-page status, upvotes, or posting history; do not judge whether the feature or joke is good.

name: Dual-Coherence Wordplay
instruction: Score whether a pun or double-meaning produces two fully coherent, self-contained readings of the sentence, each of which makes complete sense in context. A 10 means both meanings are natural, grammatically complete, and contextually appropriate—the reader can genuinely read it either way. A 0 means there is only one natural reading and the second meaning is forced, grammatically broken, or requires ignoring context to work.

name: Sourcing-versus-origination traces in the text
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the text shows signs of having been transcribed, translated, or lifted from somewhere else rather than composed for this post. Raise the score for: quoted blocks with attribution, citations, or source references; reported-speech framing that credits another teller ('I heard...', 'my friend told me', 'someone said'); dialogue rendered as a transcript with speaker labels or quotation marks; phrasing that reads as translated or non-native in its article, preposition or word-order choices; stand-up cadence or a set-up aside addressed to a live room; formatting residue such as bold or italic markers, asterisks around a title, or a stray URL or domain string. 0 = reads as written on the spot for this post, first-person and unattributed; 10 = explicitly quoted, cited, or transcribed from an external source. Score the provenance trace visible in the text only, and do NOT judge originality, plagiarism, or quality.

name: No self-explanation or apology attached to the pun
instruction: Score whether the text lets the joke land unassisted. 10 = the punchline is delivered and nothing follows; the reader is trusted to notice. 5 = a brief flourish follows that adds something of its own. 0 = the text announces that a pun has occurred, names the device, or apologizes for the joke's quality.

name: Ends on a short final line
instruction: Score 0-10 for how short the last line is relative to the rest of the text -- a clipped closing line set off on its own scores high, a final line as long as the body scores low. 10 = the final line is a few words on its own; 0 = there is no distinct short closing line. Count the layout only; do not judge whether the ending works.

name: Taboo transformed
instruction: Score 10 when a dark, political, sexual, or offensive premise is transformed by a specific clever mechanism rather than relying mainly on shock or insult; score 0 when provocation is the entire joke.

name: Brevity: punchline arrives within ~25 words with no filler
instruction: Score economy: how quickly the text reaches its payoff with no throat-clearing. 10 = complete setup-and-punch in under ~25 words with every word doing work; 0 = rambling or truncated with no payoff.

name: Self-referential platform/subreddit meta-humor
instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the joke's comedic content is *about* r/jokes, Reddit, posting, karma, upvotes, or the act of joke-telling itself, rather than about an external topic. 10 = the entire joke is a self-aware commentary on the subreddit/platform or its own reception as a post (e.g., mocking its own upvote prospects, describing addiction to Reddit, complaining about the sub's quality). 0 = no reference whatsoever to Reddit, subreddits, posting, karma, or the joke's own status as a post.

name: Insider knowledge gate with a self-verifying payoff
instruction: Score the degree to which the joke requires a specific technical, scientific, mathematical or subcultural fact to decode, AND the payoff enacts that fact rather than merely mentioning it. 10 = decoding demands real domain knowledge and the punchline is a live demonstration of the very property invoked (a joke about an unreliable protocol that may not arrive; a number that is literally the square root of another). 5 = domain vocabulary appears but the gag reduces to a generic pun any reader could get. 0 = no specialist knowledge is needed or invoked at any point.
